column1: # Flake inputs whose sibling checkout the auto-override arm provably cannot
# reach, and which are deliberately left that way for now.
# Read by scripts/check_dev_shell_env.sh (check 3). Columns:
#   <input name>
# where <kind> is one of the two ways the arm misses a sibling:
#   unreachable — the sibling exists under the REPOSITORY's name, but the
#                 input name does not strip to it, so `.envrc`'s auto arm is
#                 looking for a directory that does not exist. Fixable here,
#                 today, by renaming the input.
#   unflakeable — the names agree and the sibling exists, but it has no
#                 `flake.nix`, which the plugin requires before it will emit
#                 an `--override-input`. Not fixable here.
# An entry is a STATEMENT WITH A NAME ON IT, not a suppression. Check 3 fails
# on a finding with no entry AND on an entry that no longer describes a
# finding, so neither a new instance nor a stale excuse can sit here quietly.
# A missing file is not an empty file: with no entries at all, every finding is
# undeclared and the gate refuses.
# A ROW DESCRIBES A SIBLING THAT IS ON DISK, NOT AN INPUT THAT IS PINNED. Both
# kinds above begin with "the sibling exists", so an input whose sibling is not
# checked out beside this repository produces no finding at all.
# THIS FILE IS THEREFORE THE UNION ACROSS WORKSPACE SHAPES, NOT A SNAPSHOT OF
# ONE. It used to be read as a snapshot, and that made it unsatisfiable:
# `nim-results-src` and `nim-stew-src` sat here as `unflakeable` while neither
# `../nim-results` nor `../nim-stew` existed on `dev` or in the set
# `.github/sibling-repos` clones, so the stale-declaration arm failed on both
# in CI; they were removed on 2026-09-01 to fix that, and from that day every
# CodeTracer-flavoured workspace — which DOES check both out — failed the other
# way, on two undeclared findings. Same file, opposite polarities, no possible
# content. Because the pre-commit hook runs `just lint`, which runs this check,
# the practical result was that reprobuild accepted no commit at all in such a
# workspace.
# The stale-declaration arm is shape-aware as of 2026-09-04: a row whose
# sibling is not checked out here describes a workspace other than this one, is
# reported by name in the check's summary, and is not treated as decay. A row
# whose sibling IS here and which no longer produces a finding still fails,
# because that row really has stopped describing anything. So a row belongs
# here as soon as ANY workspace shape produces the finding, and the rows below
# are read only by the shapes they apply to.
# A ROW MUST DESCRIBE A FINDING SOME SHAPE ACTUALLY PRODUCES. Two workspaces
# can hold the same sibling at different REVISIONS — one before the commit
# that added its flake.nix and one after — and only the older one produces a
# finding. That split is not a reason to keep a row: it is a reason to stop
# cloning the revision that predates the fix, so every shape resolves and the
# row is simply unnecessary. `nim-shm-gset-src` was exactly this case and was
# closed that way, by moving the `.github/sibling-repos` pin past dc9f239.
# All three columns are required, and the check refuses a row without a reason
# or with a kind it does not recognise. That is not pedantry about format: a
# two-column row parsed fine and silenced its finding outright, which is the
# one way to make this gate pass while the defect it reports is still there.
# The defect this whole check exists for was `stackable-hooks-src`: input name
# stripping to `stackable-hooks` while the checkout is `../nim-stackable-hooks`,
# so it alone kept building from a lock pin 30 commits behind the working tree
# every other input tracked — across the commit that added the
# `WindowsInjectionResult` fields io-mon's Windows arm reads. It is fixed by
# renaming, which is why it is not in this file.
nim-shm-queue-src
column3: ../nim-shm-queue has no flake.nix, and the plugin refuses a sibling that is not a flake. Not fixable here; it needs a flake.nix in nim-shm-queue. reprobuild reaches shm_queue only through io_mon's --path, so the pinned source is what both the dev shell and CI compile.

column1: nim-stew-src
column3: ../nim-stew has no flake.nix, so the plugin will not emit an --override-input for it and the input builds from its pin. Only CodeTracer-flavoured workspaces check it out; `.github/sibling-repos` does not clone it, so CI never produces this finding — which is why the row is passed over there rather than failing as stale. NOT fixed by adding a flake.nix upstream, because it is not the same case: the input pins `status-im/nim-stew`, an upstream this organisation does not own, while `../nim-stew` is the `metacraft-labs/nim-stew` fork whose other workspace branch (`codetracer`) carries patches the pin deliberately does not have. Making it override would switch reprobuild's stew from the upstream revision it pins to whatever branch that checkout happens to sit on — a change of WHAT is compiled, which wants its own change and its own build, exactly like ct-trace-format-src below. reprobuild reaches stew only through the Nim --path seeded from this input.

column1: nim-results-src
column3: ../nim-results has no flake.nix, so the plugin will not emit an --override-input for it. Only CodeTracer-flavoured workspaces check it out; `.github/sibling-repos` does not clone it. Stronger than the nim-stew-src case above: the sibling is not the same REPOSITORY as the input. The input pins `metacraft-labs/nim-result` at df8113dd; `../nim-results` is a checkout of `arnetheduck/nim-results`, the upstream, which this organisation does not own and cannot add a flake.nix to. The auto arm pairs them only because the input name strips to that directory name, so "make it override" here would substitute one repository's source for another's rather than refresh the pinned one. Declared, not fixed.

column1: ct-trace-format-src
column3: SECOND LIVE INSTANCE of the stackable-hooks defect, found by this check on the day it was added and deliberately not fixed in the same change. The input strips to `ct-trace-format`; the repository is `codetracer-trace-format-nim`, and it IS checked out beside us WITH a flake.nix, so renaming the input to `codetracer-trace-format-nim-src` would immediately switch reprobuild's trace-format source from the pin to the working tree. That is not a refresh: the sibling sits on a branch from which the pinned bc7c5d25 is not even reachable, so the rename changes WHAT is compiled. It wants its own change, with its own build and its own gates.

column1: nimcrypto-src
column3: ../nimcrypto has no flake.nix, so the plugin will not emit an --override-input for it and the input builds from its pin. Same shape as nim-stew-src above and benign for the same reason and one more: the input pins `cheatfate/nimcrypto`, an upstream this organisation does not own and cannot add a flake.nix to, AND the sibling that is on disk is a checkout of that same upstream sitting on exactly the pinned revision (69eec037), so there is no skew for an override to close -- the two spellings already name the same source. `.github/sibling-repos` does not clone it, so CI never produces this finding; only workspaces that happen to have nimcrypto checked out for another consumer do. Declared, not fixed.
